sonnet.problem: The joke about a 25-cent sticker has nothing to do with Pharaoh being pictured as a lion and a sea monster. It doesn't share the same core action, and a baker who doesn't know the backstory would say 'huh?'. The line also never says what the sticker was on.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it. ... Bakers may not know anything about his story. Anything from his backstory ... is said in the line itself

sonnet.problem: This card tells Pharaoh being drawn up in God's net, the start of the violent judgment that leads to his slaughter. It adds a joke comparing that to Papa Dorin's own fall from the counter to the junk drawer.
sonnet.rule: A card that tells death, violence, abuse, serious sin or the body's private matters has no joke.

sonnet.problem: This story card only repeats that God darkens every shining light and brings darkness on the land. Card 13 just asked about this (verses 7-8), so it works as a recap card and moves nothing forward.
The statement tests two claims: that the most ruthless nation ravages Egypt's pride, and that all her multitudes are destroyed. Its first sentence also repeats the answer to card 5 on the same verse.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The question says "what does He say they will know?" but never says who "they" are. Verse 15 gives no antecedent, and the question names none, so the baker can't tell who "they" points to.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.
